\section[der Geschäftsführer]{der Geschäftsführer — the manager, the managing director}

\label{lesson:GE-C432-geschaeftsfuehrer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to grumble, then the German for dissatisfied.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: der Geschäftsführer}
\textbf{der Geschäftsführer} — \textquotedblleft{}the manager, the managing director\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Der Gast möchte mit dem Geschäftsführer sprechen.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The guest would like to speak to the manager.}
\end{quote}

Same form in the plural. A woman: \emph{die Geschäftsführerin}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Geschäftsführer} is built from \emph{Geschäft} 'business', inherited from Old High German \emph{giscaft} (EtymDB), and \emph{Führer} 'leader', from \emph{führen} 'to lead'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{der Geschäftsführer}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{der Geschäftsführer}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{der Geschäftsführer}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for to grumble, then the German for dissatisfied, then say \emph{der Geschäftsführer} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does der Geschäftsführer mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The manager, the managing director\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[die Unannehmlichkeit]{die Unannehmlichkeit — the inconvenience, the trouble}

\label{lesson:GE-C432-unannehmlichkeit}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for dissatisfied, then the German for the manager.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: die Unannehmlichkeit}
\textbf{die Unannehmlichkeit} — \textquotedblleft{}the inconvenience, the trouble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Wir entschuldigen uns für die Unannehmlichkeiten.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We apologise for the inconvenience.}
\end{quote}

Mostly plural: \emph{die Unannehmlichkeiten}, in a polite set phrase.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Unannehmlichkeit} is built from \emph{un-}, \emph{annehmlich} 'agreeable', from \emph{annehmen} 'to accept', and \emph{-keit}; \emph{nehmen} is inherited from Proto-Germanic \emph{nemaną}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{die Unannehmlichkeit}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{die Unannehmlichkeit}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for dissatisfied, then the German for the manager, then say \emph{die Unannehmlichkeit} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[die Anzahlung]{die Anzahlung — the deposit, the down payment}

\label{lesson:GE-C432-anzahlung}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for the manager, then the German for the inconvenience.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: die Anzahlung}
\textbf{die Anzahlung} — \textquotedblleft{}the deposit, the down payment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Für das Zimmer zahlen wir eine Anzahlung von hundert Euro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We pay a deposit of a hundred euros for the room.}
\end{quote}

Plural: \emph{die Anzahlungen}. The rest is paid later.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Anzahlung} is built from \emph{anzahlen} 'to pay part of', from \emph{zahlen} 'to pay', which comes from \emph{Zahl} 'number', inherited from Old High German \emph{zala} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for the manager, then the German for the inconvenience, then say \emph{die Anzahlung} again
\end{itemize}

\section[entschädigen]{entschädigen — to compensate}

\label{lesson:GE-C432-entschaedigen}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for the inconvenience, then the German for the deposit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: entschädigen}
\textbf{entschädigen} — \textquotedblleft{}to compensate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Das Hotel entschädigt uns mit einer Nacht gratis.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The hotel compensates us with a free night.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Jemanden für etwas entschädigen} — to compensate someone for something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{entschädigen} is built from \emph{ent-} 'away' and \emph{Schaden} 'damage', an inherited Germanic word (EtymDB lists both): to take the damage away.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{entschädigen}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{entschädigen}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for the inconvenience, then the German for the deposit, then say \emph{entschädigen} again
\end{itemize}

\section[die Entschädigung]{die Entschädigung — the compensation}

\label{lesson:GE-C432-entschaedigung}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for the deposit, then the German for to compensate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: die Entschädigung}
\textbf{die Entschädigung} — \textquotedblleft{}the compensation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Als Entschädigung bekommen wir ein besseres Zimmer.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{As compensation we get a better room.}
\end{quote}

Plural: \emph{die Entschädigungen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Entschädigung} is built on \emph{entschädigen} with \emph{-ung}; the verb comes from \emph{ent-} and \emph{Schaden} 'damage' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
